Load library(reactableEdit); existing R function names, widget bindings, JavaScript APIs, reactable.* options unchanged. Original authors, copyright notices, third-party licenses retained. Earlier release sections describe upstream reactable history.

title: reactableEdit 0.4.5.9000 (Unreleased)
text: Added comprehensive editing guide covering native Shiny inputs, stable custom IDs, modules, individual observers, native updaters, explicit server validation, disabled rules, row actions, rich tooltips, persistence troubleshooting, complete runnable Shiny application.

title: reactableEdit 0.4.5.9000 (Unreleased)
text: Native Shiny cell editing colDef(editable = TRUE), six input types (text, number, select, checkbox, date, textarea), stable row keys via reactable(rowId = ...), customizable input IDs, explicit server acceptance rejection via getReactableEdit() resolveReactableEdit(). Accepted edits display customizable status (editStatus), green tick 2 seconds default (editStatusDuration). Previous success errors clear new input. Columns can opt server validation editValidation = FALSE without displaying validation tick. Native input[[id]] observers update*Input() functions work mounted cells. Editing preserves table state initially limited client-side Shiny tables without .subRows data. Add remove rows Shiny rowActions = list(add = TRUE, remove = TRUE). Handle server requests getReactableRowAction() supply complete rows using addReactableRow(), optionally overriding new cell input IDs. Appended rows remain visible outside sorting, filtering, grouping pagination full data replacement. Removal requires confirmation, notifies server immediately, can disabled per row. Requires stable row keys client-side tables without .subRows Crosstalk data. Rich noninteractive tooltips cells, native editable inputs (including disabled inputs), column headers via reactableTooltip(), colDef(tooltip = ..., headerTooltip = ...), stable-key tooltips rules reactable() updateReactable(). Use updateReactableTooltip() override mounted input’s help ID. Tooltips support hover, keyboard focus, Escape dismissal, viewport-aware positioning custom CSS; rules per-input overrides survive pagination, virtual scrolling data replacement. Disable native cell inputs column colDef(inputDisabled = TRUE), stable row key, column, cell using disabledInputs reactable() updateReactable(). Cell exceptions can enable otherwise disabled inputs. Use updateReactableInput() native input messages mounted cells; external DOM changes shinyjs::disable() also persist across remounts. Disabling discards unsent drafts without interrupting pending server responses. Experimental support server-side data processing Shiny apps. Use reactable(server = TRUE) render table using server-side data processing Shiny. Server-side data processing requires V8 package, installed reactable default. (#22) reactable() gains virtual argument enable virtual scrolling. Virtual scrolling renders visible rows screen, allowing scroll large tables without performance issues. (#203) New Reactable.toggleSortBy() Reactable.setSortBy() methods JavaScript API programmatically control column sorting. toggleSortBy() toggles sort single column (cycling ascending descending), setSortBy() sets full sort state declaratively. Also available via updateReactable(sortBy = ...) Shiny. (#316, #322) New Reactable.toggleRowSelected(), Reactable.setRowsSelected(), Reactable.toggleAllRowsSelected() methods JavaScript API programmatically control row selection. Additionally, rowInfo.toggleRowSelected() cellInfo.toggleRowSelected() now available JavaScript render style functions. (#322, #394, #412) New Reactable.gotoPage() Reactable.setPageSize() methods JavaScript API change current page page size. (#322) JSON serialization data can now customized using reactable.json.func option. experimental feature advanced use , intentionally undocumented outside NEWS. reactable may change data serialized versions guarantee stability. See reactableEdit:::toJSON reference data currently serialized. (@khusmann, #415) Example usage: colDef() gains initWidth argument set column’s initial width pixels keeping column resizable. Unlike width, sets fixed width disables resizing, initWidth sets starting width, column can still resized within minWidth maxWidth. (@nteetor, #223, #374)
code: library(shiny) library(reactableEdit)  tbl <- reactable(   mtcars,   server = TRUE )  ui <- fluidPage(   reactableOutput("tbl") )  server <- function(input, output) {   output$tbl <- renderReactable({     tbl   }) }  shinyApp(ui, server) reactable(   data.frame(x = 1:100000, y = rnorm(100000)),   pagination = FALSE,   virtual = TRUE,   height = 500 ) # Use yyjsonr as a faster alternative for JSON serialization. Note that this is not 1:1 consistent with # jsonlite, and several edge cases are not handled here, including data frames with 1 row, datetimes, and NULLs. options(reactable.json.func = function(x, ...) {   result <- yyjsonr::write_json_str(     x,     opts = yyjsonr::opts_write_json(       dataframe = "columns",       auto_unbox = TRUE,       num_specials = "string"     )   )   class(result) <- "json"   result })

title: reactableEdit 0.4.5.9000 (Unreleased)
text: Improved rendering performance large tables. Fixed inconsistent spacing column group borders resizable tables. (@wvictor14, #396) Fixed JS() working htmlwidgets 1.6.3 later installed. (#348) reactableTheme(), stripedColor highlightColor now work using sticky columns. (@grcatlin, #401) Crosstalk tables, pagination longer resets selecting row page greater 1. (@msaltieri, #349) Shiny apps, tables now update correctly reactive meta values change. (@khusmann, #416) Fixed pagination showing incorrect page buttons (e.g., “1 2 3 4 5 NaN”) using pagination = FALSE showPagination = TRUE filtering rows.

title: reactableEdit 0.4.5.9000 (Unreleased)
text: Internet Explorer 11 (IE 11) longer supported. core-js longer included HTML dependencies. required support IE 11 old versions RStudio Viewer. (#245) meta now converted JavaScript way data, using reactable’s internal JSON serialization function rather htmlwidgets’s JSON serialization function. breaking change rare cases, major difference numeric NA, NaN, Inf, -Inf values now serialized strings preserved, rather always converted null. (@khusmann, #415)
